correctness.rationale: The p=1 matrix is identity plus a path Laplacian, hence a nonsingular irreducible M-matrix whose inverse is strictly positive; constants are fixed, giving stochastic rows and exact range preservation. For every p>=2, the minimal n=p+1 penalty is rank one and Sherman-Morrison gives an explicit negative p-2 coordinate on a terminal step for every lambda>0. An affine nullspace perturbation yields strict positive increasing witnesses. Exact rational replay verifies the finite algebra.

originality.rationale: The literature already contains the Whittaker-Henderson normal equations, explicit order-one weights, and exact Hodrick-Prescott weight formulas; these are excluded from novelty. The accepted claim is the all-order range-preservation dichotomy and the minimal-length every-smoothing-strength obstruction for every p>=2. Required semantic-index and primary-literature searches did not locate an implication-equivalent theorem.
residual_risks: The p=1 explicit-weight literature may make positivity an immediate corollary; that side is not claimed as a new formula.
An older graduation or positive-linear-operator source may state the same order dichotomy under different terminology.
The full text of Eilers 2003 was not inspected because the publisher required human verification after OA alternatives failed.
Weighted or irregular-grid Whittaker-Henderson variants are outside the claim.

value.rationale: Difference order is a central user choice in Whittaker-Henderson smoothing. The result gives a complete structural safety classification, proves failure at the smallest possible sample length and arbitrarily weak smoothing, and provides symbolic strict witnesses useful for diagnostics and for deciding when constrained smoothing is necessary.
